claims.text: The 5.00 SGD is already off the rider's side of the ledger, and the driver's filing is an attempt to put it back. The payments ledger records refund_issued_sgd 5.00 with payment_status REFUNDED and a single cancellation-fee line reconciled to the total charged (EV-FARE-05067), and the trip record carries the platform's fee_reversed event at 2026-09-13T10:46:10, 'refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' (EV-TRIP-05067). POL-GEN-03 defines NO_ACTION as the filing party's claim not being supported and the present state standing, and it is party-relative and 'never means restore a charge'. The driver is the filer here, so the 5.00 can move back to him only if his own claim is affirmatively made out; unless it is, the refund already issued to the rider stands and the amounts on the ruling are null.

This trip is on-demand and the record fixes no scheduled pickup time at all: scheduled_at is null and the derived driver_deadline is null, with the stated reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time' (EV-TRIP-05067). POL-NS-24's test is the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, so on this record that deadline cannot be fixed, and POL-NS-24's own reading of v2.1 sends the case to POL-GEN-26 where the deadline cannot be fixed. POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated rather than an outcome inferred, and POL-GEN-03 makes an escalation terminal and holds the amount — so the 5.00 stays credited to the rider and withheld from the driver instead of being released to him as compensation.

The charge POL-NS-22 authorises is a no-show fee, and this record does not show the rider failing to appear. She read every message the driver sent — MSG-05067-001, -002 and -003 read at 09:22:42, 09:25:37 and 09:29:09, each within about a minute of sending (EV-CHAT-05067) — so she was on her phone and available throughout the free wait POL-NS-21 gives her to come out and board, and her account on file is that she was downstairs waiting. The GPS artifact carries no rider track at all (rider_track empty; the only trace is the driver's own device, EV-GPS-05067), so nothing in the record contradicts her account. The no-show premise on which the driver would take the 5.00 as compensation is not made out on this evidence, and the refund already issued should stand.

Nothing on a profile can decide this trip. POL-GEN-22 confines a fraud flag to raising the confidence an AI ruling needs — it never decides the trip — and POL-GEN-01 forbids every other profile field from establishing a fact about this trip. The rider's snapshot carries fraud_flags 3 (EV-RPROF-05067), so the required confidence for any ruling here is 0.95 whatever the dispute value (POL-GEN-22, carried into no-shows by POL-NS-26), and the driver's claim to take back an already-refunded 5.00 must clear that bar; the rider's rating, cancellation history and prior disputes are context only and cannot be used to reimpose the fee.

The free-wait precondition to a no-show cancellation is met. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled_at on the record, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival: the trip record auto-arrived the driver at 09:21:45, the timer therefore expired at 09:26:45 ('wait_timer_expired' at 09:26:50), and the driver did not cancel until 09:30:10 — 505 s after arrival and roughly 205 s past the expiry of the free wait, with the rider still not on board.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is satisfied on both limbs, not just one. Before the 09:30:10 cancellation the driver sent three in-app chat messages (09:22:00 'reached Blk 680 drop-off point, white Vezel'; 09:25:30 'waiting downstairs'; 09:28:40 'Going to cancel in 1 min if no reply ya') and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, rang 30 s; 09:27:20, rang 25 s), each call unanswered. The chat log shows each message was delivered (09:22:02, 09:25:32, 09:28:43) and read by the rider (09:22:42, 09:25:37, 09:29:09). Every element of the clause is present, so nothing in POL-NS-23 voids the fee.

The arrival event is corroborated by the driver's own trace, which is what POL-NS-21's arrival test requires. The nearest GPS fix to the pickup point is 1.81 m away — far inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone — and from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50 the trace reports a continuous run of fixes at 0 kph, i.e. the vehicle was stationary at the pickup for the whole free wait and beyond. Against that, the rider's counterparty statement that 'the driver never came to my block' is uncorroborated: the GPS payload carries no rider track at all. The only track on the record confirms the driver's presence.

POL-NS-24 cannot be turned against the driver on this record. That clause bites only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes; this booking was on-demand and carries no scheduled_at, and POL-NS-21 expressly directs that on an on-demand trip the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, which the record fixes at 09:21:45. There is no scheduled deadline the driver is shown to have missed, so the rider's no-charge cancellation route under POL-NS-24 is not open and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under that clause arises.

The fee itself is policy-correct. The payments ledger records a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 09:30:14, fee_matches_policy true, and a policy fee of 5.00 SGD. Under POL-NS-22, where the driver cancels after the free wait the 5.00 SGD fee is charged to the rider and transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, and where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both amount fields equal to the fee charged. The driver's case is that ruling: 5.00 SGD to the driver.

The 10:46:10 entry in the trip record is an interim measure taken after the rider's complaint, not a finding on the merits: the record describes it as 'SGD 5.00 refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review'. POL-GEN-03 is explicit that DRIVER_COMPENSATION means the driver is owed money, and that amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd. Nothing about the interim reversal makes the fee invalid; it is precisely the state the driver asks this tribunal to correct.

POL-GEN-26 has no work to do here. Every fact the no-show rules need — arrival, the length of the free wait, the messages and calls before cancellation, and the fee charged — is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired. The one MISSING artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05067-01, carries weight 0.0, holds no payload, and bears on no element of POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 or POL-NS-23, so its absence leaves no open question and cannot ground an escalation.

The confidence the AI ruling needs is available. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3, so POL-GEN-22 raises the required confidence to 0.95 for this 5.00 SGD dispute. The driver's case rests on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the payments ledger, all four graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 by the pre-pass, so the deciding facts are carried by clean evidence and the 0.95 requirement is met.

To both parties: the no-show fee was correctly charged, so the interim refund to the rider is reversed in the driver's favour.

The conditions for the fee are all met on complete evidence. This was an on-demand booking (scheduled_at is null), so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival: the trip record auto-arrives him at 09:21:45 and the wait expired at 09:26:45, and he did not cancel until 09:30:10 — after the wait, with the rider not on board. The arrival event is corroborated by the driver's own GPS trace (nearest fix 1.81 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; the trace shows the vehicle stationary from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50). The POL-NS-23 contact obligation is satisfied on both limbs: three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and two in-app calls (09:24:10, rang 30 s; 09:27:20, rang 25 s), every one placed before the 09:30:10 cancellation. The fare breakdown records a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line matching the policy fee of 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22).

The rider's account that 'the driver never came to my block' is not accepted. It is uncorroborated — the GPS payload carries no rider track at all, and the only trace on the record places the driver at the pickup throughout the wait — and the chat log shows she read all three of the driver's messages (09:22:42, 09:25:37, 09:29:09), so she was available and simply did not board within the free wait. No clause makes the rider's statement the test of any limb here, and nothing in POL-NS-23 voids the fee.

The rider's request to escalate under POL-GEN-26 is not accepted. The facts the operative rules need — when the driver arrived, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and the fee charged — are each carried by COMPLETE, weight-1.0 artifacts, and POL-NS-21 supplies the on-demand timing from the driver's arrival, so no scheduled pickup time is required to decide this fee. POL-NS-24's scheduled-plus-5 deadline is not a fact POL-NS-21 or POL-NS-22 needs in order to operate, and the driver is not shown to have missed any arrival obligation.

The entry at 10:46:10 was an interim reversal 'pending review', not a merits finding, so the present state is not the correct one. POL-GEN-03's NO_ACTION applies where the filing party's claim is not supported; here the driver's claim is made out, so it is he who is owed the 5.00 SGD. Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22, POL-GEN-03).

No referral arises. The fee is 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire; the driver did arrive and did make contact, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises; and the rider's no-show count with this trip would be 2, below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3.

On confidence: the deciding facts rest on artifacts graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3, which raises the required confidence to 0.95 under POL-GEN-22 (carried into no-shows by POL-NS-26); the ruling meets that bar at 0.95. The rider is right that the flag itself never decides the trip — it does not here; the outcome rests on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the payments ledger.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides' claims are answered below.

THE NO-SHOW FEE WAS CORRECTLY CHARGED, SO THE DRIVER IS OWED THE 5.00 SGD. On this on-demand booking there is no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The driver auto-arrived at Block 680 at 09:21:45, corroborated by his own GPS trace: the nearest fix is 1.81 m from the pickup point, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace reports the vehicle stationary at 0 kph from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50. The free wait expired at 09:26:45 and the driver did not cancel until 09:30:10 — 505 s after arrival. Before cancelling he sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10 and 09:27:20, both unanswered), all before the 09:30:10 cancellation, so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is satisfied on both limbs and nothing there voids the fee. The fare breakdown records a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, matching the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22 applies and the fee stands.

THE RIDER'S ACCOUNT DOES NOT DEFEAT THE ARRIVAL TEST. The rider says the driver never came to her block and that she was downstairs waiting. That statement is not corroborated — the GPS artifact carries no rider track at all — and it does not displace the POL-NS-21 arrival test, which the trip record and the driver's trace satisfy. She read each message within about a minute, but the record shows she did not board during the free wait, and the no-show fee POL-NS-22 authorises does not depend on anything beyond the free wait and the contact obligation.

THE RIDER'S ESCALATION ARGUMENT IS REJECTED. The rider argues that POL-NS-24's deadline (scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes) cannot be fixed on an on-demand trip and that the case must therefore go to POL-GEN-26. POL-NS-24 protects the rider where the DRIVER is late on a scheduled trip; the driver here arrived promptly and the rider did not cancel, so that clause's route is not engaged. POL-NS-21 expressly fixes the free wait from arrival for an on-demand trip, so the deadline is determinable, and no fact the no-show rules need is missing: the arrival, the length of the wait, the messages and calls before cancellation, and the fee charged are all carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0. The one MISSING artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05067-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), bears on no element of POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 or POL-NS-23, so its absence opens no question and grounds no escalation.

THE INTERIM REVERSAL IS NOT A FINDING. The 10:46:10 fee_reversed entry is the platform's interim measure after the rider's complaint — 'refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' — not a decision on the merits. Because the fee stands on the evidence, the rider's 5.00 SGD refund does not stand, and under POL-NS-22 with POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying the 5.00 SGD the ruling moves.

CONFIDENCE. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags 3, so POL-GEN-22 (carried into no-shows by POL-NS-26) requires confidence of 0.95. The deciding facts rest on the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown, all graded COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the bar is met at 0.96.

REFERRALS. None fires. The fee charged (5.00 SGD) equals the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not apply; the driver did arrive, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit (which needs a failed arrival AND a failed contact attempt) does not arise; and the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d of 1, counting this trip, is 2, below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee is valid, and because the driver filed to contest the refund already given to the rider, the 5.00 SGD is returned to the driver.

Why the fee stands. This was an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second (5-minute) free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05067) puts the auto-arrival at 09:21:45, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05067) corroborates it - the nearest fix is 1.81 m from the pickup, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 09:21:50 onward. The free wait expired at 09:26:45 and the driver cancelled at 09:30:10, 505 seconds after arrival, with the rider not on board. Nothing is missing or impaired here: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and payments ledger are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on both limbs: three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), every one of them before the 09:30:10 cancellation. The fee is therefore not voided, and the 5.00 SGD is exactly the policy fee (fee_matches_policy true), so POL-NS-22's amount check does not fire.

The rider's answers do not change this. Her account that 'the driver never came to my block' is contradicted by the driver's own trace, and the GPS artifact carries no rider track (rider_track empty), so the record does not support it; POL-NS-21 requires only that she not be on board after the free wait, which she was not, and that the wait ran from arrival. POL-NS-24 does not help her: it gives a rider a free cancellation only if the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and here the driver did arrive, so there is no missed deadline to fix and no unestablished fact for POL-GEN-26 to escalate - the arrival, the wait, the messages and calls, and the fee are all carried by clean artifacts. Her point on profiles is correct as far as it goes: the rider's fraud_flags of 3 raise the confidence required to 0.95 (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26) and POL-GEN-01 keeps every other profile field (rating, prior disputes, cancellation history) context only - but this case is decided on the trip evidence, not on any profile.

No referral arises: POL-NS-22's amount check does not fire (fee is the policy 5.00 SGD); POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise (the driver both arrived and made contact); and the rider's no-show count with this trip standing is 2, below POL-NS-25's threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
The SGD 5.00 no-show fee and the SGD 5.00 already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver are held; this case must go to a human reviewer, because one fact the no-show rules need cannot be fixed on this record.

To the driver: on the evidence, your no-show looks procedurally sound. The trip record auto-arrived you at 09:21:45 and the nearest GPS fix was 1.81 m from the Block 680 pickup, well inside the 50 m arrival radius, with the trace reporting a continuous run of 0 kph fixes from 09:21:50 to 09:29:50 (POL-NS-21). This was an on-demand trip, so the 300 s free wait ran from your arrival and expired at 09:26:45; you cancelled at 09:30:10, 505 s after arrival. Before cancelling you sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20, both unanswered), so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met, and the SGD 5.00 fee charged at 09:30:14 matches the policy fee (POL-NS-22).

To the rider: your account that the driver never came to your block is not corroborated by any rider-side trace — the only GPS on file is the driver's own device — and it does not displace the POL-NS-21 arrival test, which reads the trip record's arrival event corroborated by the GPS trace. That the messages were delivered and read does not establish that you boarded.

Why the case cannot be decided here: POL-NS-24 gives a rider a no-charge route where the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes. This booking was on-demand and the record carries no scheduled pickup time (scheduled_at is null; the derived driver deadline is null, reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), so that deadline cannot be fixed. POL-NS-24's own reading sends this situation to POL-GEN-26, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated rather than an outcome inferred from the absence of evidence. The interim reversal at 10:46:10 is therefore neither confirmed nor undone here.

No referral issues: POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire (the driver made contact), POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire (the rider's count is 1, below the threshold of 3), and POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire (the fee charged is the policy 5.00 SGD). Open question for the reviewer: whether an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time can support a POL-NS-24 no-charge route at all, and whether the rider's uncorroborated account should outweigh the driver's corroborated arrival.
